source.title: Trump says Musk has restored access to Ukraine's Starlink network
source.summary: Ukraine relies on Starlink for a range of military uses - its owner Elon Musk has repeatedly denied restricting access.
source.evidence_text:
Ukraine relies on Starlink for a range of military uses - its owner Elon Musk has repeatedly denied restricting access.
Modern warfare often relies on the use of high-speed internet to effectively operate drones.
Earlier on Thursday, Zelensky said the speed of the system used by Ukraine's military had still not been restored fully.
The speed limit made Ukraine's offensive drones and interceptors powerless against Russian attacks.
Elon Musk has restored Ukraine's Starlink internet access, US President Donald Trump has said, after restrictions hampered Kyiv's armed forces.
The journal reported that the system was working more normally on Thursday, shortly after their conversation.
Trump made the comments after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said connectivity to the military-grade Starshield network, which is provided by Musk's satellite-based Starlink system, had yet to be fully restored.
Trump refused to be drawn on a report that he had called Musk to ask him to lift restrictions to the service, but said: "Bottom line, he put it back."
Musk said last week that the US government ultimately controls access to Starshield, the military-grade version of Starlink which Ukraine uses for some of its operation. He said the system was designed for the Pentagon, suggesting the US military may therefore be behind the restrictions.
The connectivity restrictions came as Trump put pressure on Zelensky to stop Ukrainian attacks on Russian oil refineries, which he has argued have caused prices to rise.
Faced with midterm elections next month, Trump has waived some sanctions on Russia and agreed a deal to import Russian diesel for the US market - a move criticised by Ukraine and its European allies.
The US outlet reported that Trump told Musk he was frustrated the Starlink system's speeds were still capped at around 160km/h, according to officials.
Musk previously denied he was behind the slowdown, which affects Ukraine's ability to use drones to attack Russian targets in Ukraine and protect itself from attacks.
The White House has repeatedly said it did not order access to be restricted.

news_brief_sentences: US President Donald Trump claims that Elon Musk has reactivated full access to Ukraine’s satellite internet network, following reports that deliberate limitations had severely hampered Kyiv's tactical maneuvers.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky previously noted that connectivity to the highly secure Starshield network, provided by Musk's infrastructure, had yet to be fully re-established.
The connectivity limitations coincided with Trump pressuring Zelensky to halt Ukrainian aerial strikes on Russian oil refineries, which the US leader argued were causing global prices to surge.
Facing crucial midterm elections next month, Trump also waived specific sanctions on Moscow and approved a controversial deal to import Russian diesel.
According to unnamed officials, Trump contacted Musk to express frustration that the network's data speeds remained severely capped.
These artificial speed limits rendered Ukraine's frontline interceptors practically useless against incoming Russian strikes.
Although Trump refused to confirm whether he directly asked Musk to lift the limitations, he confidently asserted that the service had been successfully reinstated.
For his part, Musk has consistently denied deliberately throttling the network, which is vital for targeting remote positions and protecting the country.
Furthermore, the tech entrepreneur suggested that the US government might be responsible for the limitations, as the Pentagon fundamentally controls access to the secure platform.
Nevertheless, the White House has categorically denied issuing any formal orders to curtail the crucial satellite service.
lesson.overview: Amid political pressure and tactical concerns, Donald Trump claims Elon Musk has reinstated crucial satellite network access for Ukraine's defense.
